\u003cstrong\u003epreferred\u003c/strong\u003e way to use Code Mode — no MCP server, no client config, no env vars. The agent self-configures by writing a \u003ccode\u003e.utcp_config.json\u003c/code\u003e and drives everything from the shell.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJust point the agent at the built-in guide:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli prompt\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003enpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli prompt\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eHand it a description of the API to use — a UTCP call template, an \u003cstrong\u003eOpenAPI spec\u003c/strong\u003e, or a \u003cstrong\u003eplain-English description\u003c/strong\u003e — and it writes the config, discovers tools, runs tool-chains, and even completes \u003cstrong\u003einteractive OAuth logins\u003c/strong\u003e (e.g. Notion), all from the shell:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli search \u0026quot;\u0026lt;task\u0026gt;\u0026quot;           # discover tools + TS interfaces\nnpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli run \u0026lt;\u0026lt;'EOF'               # run a tool-chain\nconst r = await openlibrary.read_search_json_search_json_get({ q: \u0026quot;tolkien\u0026quot;, limit: 3 });\nreturn r.docs.map(b =\u0026gt; b.title);\nEOF\nnpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli login \u0026lt;manual\u0026gt;            # interactive OAuth, writes token to .env\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003enpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli search \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u0026lt;task\u0026gt;\u003cspan class=\"pl-pds\"\u003e\"\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e           \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e discover tools + TS interfaces\u003c/span\u003e\nnpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli run \u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003e'\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eEOF\u003c/span\u003e'               # run a tool-chain\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003econst r = await openlibrary.read_search_json_search_json_get({ q: \"tolkien\", limit: 3 });\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003ereturn r.docs.map(b =\u0026gt; b.title);\u003c/span\u003e\n\u003cspan class=\"pl-s\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003eEOF\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/span\u003e\nnpx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli login \u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026lt;\u003c/span\u003emanual\u003cspan class=\"pl-k\"\u003e\u0026gt;\u003c/span\u003e            \u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e\u003cspan class=\"pl-c\"\u003e#\u003c/span\u003e interactive OAuth, writes token to .env\u003c/span\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eCLI vs MCP:\u003c/strong\u003e prefer the \u003cstrong\u003eCLI\u003c/strong\u003e whenever the agent has shell access (most coding agents) — it's simpler and self-configuring. Use the \u003cstrong\u003eMCP server\u003c/strong\u003e (below) only for MCP-only clients like Claude Desktop. <p dir="auto">Transform your AI agents from clunky tool callers into efficient code executors — in just 3 lines.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why This Changes Everything</h2><a id="user-content-why-this-changes-everything" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why This Changes Everything" href="#why-this-changes-everything"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">LLMs excel at writing code but struggle with tool calls. Instead of exposing hundreds of tools directly, give them ONE tool that executes TypeScript code with access to your entire toolkit.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/codeact" rel="nofollow">Apple</a>, <a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/code-mode/" rel="nofollow">Cloudflare</a>, and <a href="https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp" rel="nofollow">Anthropic</a> say that Code-Mode is a more efficient way to approach tool calling compared to the traditional dump function information and then extract a JSON for function calling.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>If your agent can run shell commands</strong> (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Claude Cowork, etc.), the <a href="/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/main/code-mode-cli"><code>utcp</code> CLI</a> is the <strong>preferred</strong> way to use Code Mode — no MCP server, no client config, no env vars. The agent self-configures by writing a <code>.utcp_config.json</code> and drives everything from the shell.</p>
<p dir="auto">Just point the agent at the built-in guide:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli prompt"><pre>npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli prompt</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Hand it a description of the API to use — a UTCP call template, an <strong>OpenAPI spec</strong>, or a <strong>plain-English description</strong> — and it writes the config, discovers tools, runs tool-chains, and even completes <strong>interactive OAuth logins</strong> (e.g. Notion), all from the shell:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli search "<task>"           # discover tools + TS interfaces
npx -y @utcp/code-mode-cli run <<'EOF'               # run a tool-chain
const r = await openlibrary.read_search_json_search_json_get({ q: "tolkien", limit: 3 });

<blockquote>
<p dir="auto">Each <code>call_template_type</code> is a separate plugin package. Install and import the

The same pattern applies to other transports: <code>@utcp/http</code>, <code>@utcp/text</code>, etc.</p>
